_comment: Concept graph for the book. owner = numbered chapter or appendix that teaches it (build-then-name). previews = earlier book units allowed to use it with a gloss + pointer. depends_on = concepts its OWNER-level definition uses. aliases = word-boundary regexes for the use-before-teach scan; scan=false skips scanning (too common a word). Maintained per AGENTS.md P6; checked by scripts/check-graph.py.

character.intuition: one ASCII byte such as a letter, digit, or space; other encodings may need several bytes for one displayed character

previews.1: position in the sorted 80-character alphabet

id.definition: the zero-based integer label assigned to one vocabulary token value
id.intuition: the compact number written beside one entry in the sorted alphabet

previews.0: one ASCII byte = one character = one token here; general encodings can differ
previews.1: Chapter 3's later name for one piece of text that receives an id; one character here

token.definition: a chunk of text treated as one indivisible model input; exactly one ASCII byte here
token.intuition: each ASCII byte occurrence is one model-sized piece; repeated byte values reuse the same id

previews.0: 80 distinct characters
previews.1: alphabet table row V

vocabulary.definition: the set of distinct token values the model can represent
vocabulary.intuition: the model's complete alphabet, with each distinct byte including space and newline written once

previews.0: the training text: NIGHT GRID, with Chapter 3 as the construction
previews.1: the text whose next characters supply the answers

corpus.definition: a deliberately selected body of text used to supply training examples
corpus.intuition: NIGHT GRID repeats headers, handles, and slang inside the 128-character span the model can study

command-environment-assignment.definition: a shell NAME=value prefix that supplies one environment variable to the following command only
command-environment-assignment.intuition: give one make invocation a larger target or give one tr invocation the C locale without changing later commands

shell-variable-assignment.definition: a standalone shell NAME=value line that keeps the value available to later lines in that shell
shell-variable-assignment.intuition: store the header pattern once, then expand it into AWK's -v argument later

previews.0: NIGHT GRID cleaning admits only permitted forms; Chapter 3 builds the exact rules

whitelist.definition: an admission rule that starts empty and keeps only explicitly permitted forms
whitelist.intuition: begin with empty output and let text through only when an accepted rule admits it

previews.0: generated NIGHT GRID text is distilled through a grammar whitelist; Chapter 3 builds the accepted shapes

corpus-grammar.definition: a stateful whitelist that emits only complete accepted scenes and caps repeated dialogue
corpus-grammar.intuition: hold a valid header until dialogue proves the scene complete, reset on a malformed header, and reject the fourth identical dialogue copy

previews.1: characters converted into compact integer ids; Chapter 3 builds the mapping

tokenization.definition: convert a sequence of text tokens into vocabulary ids
tokenization.intuition: replace each known byte occurrence with the compact number assigned to its value

previews.1: object that maps known bytes to ids and valid ids back to bytes

tokenizer.definition: the object that owns both the token-to-id and id-to-token mappings
tokenizer.intuition: write the sorted alphabet once, then use one table in each direction

previews.1: production models often assign one id to a multi-character word piece

subword-token.definition: one indivisible model token that contains a recurring sequence of text bytes
subword-token.intuition: giving th one id turns the seven byte tokens in the the into five token positions

serialization.definition: turn in-memory state into an ordered byte representation and reconstruct it later
serialization.intuition: write the tokenizer count followed by its sorted id-to-byte alphabet, then rebuild the same two tables

training-split.definition: the complete corpus records assigned to model updates by a seeded partition
training-split.intuition: shuffle whole transmissions reproducibly, then let only the unmarked records shape the model

validation-split.definition: the complementary complete records withheld from model updates for later checks
validation-split.intuition: keep the marked whole transmissions behind the no-peeking boundary and check them later

data-leakage.definition: held-out information influencing training data or training setup
data-leakage.intuition: keep each transmission on one side and build the alphabet from training bytes; canonical global cleaning still happens before this boundary

previews.0: the model's prepared training text; Chapter 3 builds its encoded form
previews.1: the module that turns corpus text into shifted input and target rows

dataset.definition: an owned array of corpus token ids from which training windows are drawn
dataset.intuition: a deck of numbered text whose overlapping windows can be dealt as training flashcards

previews.1: each input position paired with the character immediately after it

next-token-pair.definition: one input token id paired with the immediately following target token id
next-token-pair.intuition: each position on the front of a flashcard lines up with its one-token-later answer on the back

sampling-with-replacement.definition: draw each legal dataset window without removing earlier choices
sampling-with-replacement.intuition: return each flashcard to the deck after drawing it, so the same starting position may appear again

buffer-capacity.definition: the number of elements a caller has made writable behind a destination pointer
buffer-capacity.intuition: a pointer carries an address, not a length; encoding needs length slots and batching needs B times T slots in each destination

undefined-behavior.definition: a C execution outside the language's guarantees, for which no result is promised
undefined-behavior.intuition: a write past the last allocated slot may damage another object or appear to work and fail later

array-parameter.definition: a C function parameter written as T values[N] that the language adjusts to a T pointer without checking N
array-parameter.intuition: the 256 in seen[256] documents the borrowed row, but the caller still supplies all 256 elements

logical-not.definition: the C ! operator maps zero to true and every nonzero value to false
logical-not.intuition: !0 is 1 while !1 is 0, so !seen selects an unseen byte

pointer-arithmetic.definition: within one array, adding n to a typed pointer advances by n objects; one-past may be formed but not read
pointer-arithmetic.intuition: adding five to the dataset pointer reaches source position five; the legal-start proof keeps every read inside the token array

byte-copy.definition: memcpy copies a stated number of bytes between valid non-overlapping memory regions
byte-copy.intuition: point at the first integer slot, then copy block_size times the byte size of one integer

byte-fill.definition: memset repeats one byte value across a stated number of writable bytes; on the supported IEEE 754 machines, all-zero bytes represent float zero
byte-fill.intuition: write zero into every byte of one output slice before adding weighted value rows into it

row-major-storage.definition: a flat matrix layout in which one row's columns occupy consecutive elements and the next row follows immediately
row-major-storage.intuition: in a two-by-three grid, row zero uses offsets zero through two and row one begins at offset three

previews.1: Mat = pointer + rows + columns; Chapter 4 builds the small public description

mat.definition: a three-field C value containing a float-storage pointer plus row and column counts
mat.intuition: copy the three-field description while the float array stays at its original address

previews.1: a Mat is pointer + rows + columns, a view and never an owner

matrix-view.definition: a Mat description that borrows existing float storage without allocating, freeing, or copying the float payload
matrix-view.intuition: one float array keeps one owner while several copied descriptions expose it

leading-row-view.definition: a new Mat with the same base pointer and column count and a visible row count no greater than its parent
leading-row-view.intuition: a three-by-four parent and two-by-four prefix begin at the same float, so a write through the prefix reaches the parent

row-stride.definition: the element distance between starts of adjacent logical rows, equal to the column count for Mat storage
row-stride.intuition: a four-column row advances the float pointer by four to reach the next row

reshape-view.definition: a new rows-by-columns description of the same storage without moving values, valid only when the backing capacity and packing fit
reshape-view.intuition: the first four floats of a four-by-four buffer can be read as two packed rows of width two, changing the second row's start

header-guard.definition: a preprocessor condition around a header body that skips repeated definitions after the first inclusion
header-guard.intuition: the first include defines a marker and reads the body; later includes see the marker and skip the body

static-inline-header-helper.definition: a function body placed in a header with a private definition for each including C file and an inline specifier that does not determine whether calls are substituted
static-inline-header-helper.intuition: each C file gets its own tiny Mat helper, whether the compiler keeps a call or substitutes the helper body

positional-struct-initializer.definition: a brace list that initializes struct fields in their declaration order
positional-struct-initializer.intuition: the three values vals, rows, and cols enter the three Mat fields in that same declared order

struct-member-access.definition: the C dot operator selecting one named field directly from a struct value
struct-member-access.intuition: now.tv_sec selects the whole-second field while now.tv_nsec selects the remaining nanoseconds

array-to-pointer-conversion.definition: the usual C conversion of an array expression to a pointer to its first element, including when passed as a function argument
array-to-pointer-conversion.intuition: passing seen supplies &seen[0] while the 256-element array itself stays in tokenizer_new

previews.0: grade for next-character guesses on one selected group of snippets; not a running average
previews.1: one grade for all known next-character answers in a batch; lower is better and reports may bounce

loss.definition: the single scalar returned by the grading rule; here, the batch mean cross-entropy
loss.intuition: one group's grade for the next-character bets; lower is better, and reports may bounce

parameter.definition: one of the model's adjustable numbers
parameter.intuition: one of the 815,360 adjustable numbers; training is nudging them

previews.0: deliberate starting values: random weights and neutral multipliers and additions; Chapter 1 catalogs the recipe

parameter-initialization.definition: the deliberate starting value assigned to every parameter before training
parameter-initialization.intuition: before the corpus teaches anything, set most adjustable numbers near zero while learned multipliers start at one and additions start at zero

previews.0: name for the complete machine; Chapter 1 provides the map

transformer.definition: the complete route from opening rows of notes, through repeated consult-and-edit blocks, to next-character scores
transformer.intuition: rows of notes move through editing blocks until each row can produce next-character scores

previews.0: label for the finished machine; Chapter 1 builds the one-stack distinction

decoder-only.definition: a transformer with one preceding-text-to-next-character stack and no separate stack reading another source sequence
decoder-only.intuition: one stack revises the notes for the text seen so far; there is no second source-reading stack

previews.0: one run from input token ids to next-character predictions

forward-pass.definition: one call that carries input ids through the transformer to next-character scores and, when answers are supplied, continues through grading
forward-pass.intuition: training and generation call the same score route; only the training call supplies answers for the optional grade

weight.definition: synonym for a learned parameter; distinct from a temporary attention mixing weight
weight.intuition: a learned weight survives between passes; an attention weight is recomputed for one pass

previews.0: one of 5,000 training rounds in the printout; Chapter 1 maps what one round must do

step.definition: one batch, one grade, one backward calculation, and one visit to the parameter updater
step.intuition: draw known text, erase old correction signals, predict and grade, send corrections backward, then adjust parameters

matrix.definition: grid of numbers with shape rows x columns
matrix.intuition: the three-position by four-channel notes grid

shape.definition: rows by columns, always in that order
shape.intuition: rows by columns, always in that order

channel.definition: a column index; one slot of a position's notes
channel.intuition: one vertical note slot across every position row; a column index, nothing more

notes-row.definition: the model's running notes about one text position; a token's state
notes-row.intuition: the model's running notes about one position, revised block by block

batch.definition: a group of sequences graded together; B is the configured maximum
batch.intuition: several snippets graded together so one nudge draws on many corpus places

context-length.definition: T, the configured maximum positions per sequence and hard ceiling on lookback
context-length.intuition: the furthest back the model can ever look: 128 characters

model-configuration.definition: the public six-integer ModelConfig value that carries V, T, C, H, L, and B together
model-configuration.intuition: one copyable value keeps all six capacities together so every module receives the same geometry

model-configuration-validity.definition: the geometry predicate requiring positive bounded V, T, C, H, L, and B, B*T within its row ceiling, and C divisible by H
model-configuration-validity.intuition: test positive bounds, row capacity, and equal head division before any storage size is considered

flattening.definition: a full-capacity B x T x C batch stored as (B*T) x C = R x C
flattening.intuition: stack the B note-grids into one tall grid; bookkeeping, not a merge

vector.definition: an ordered list of numbers read as one row
vector.intuition: one short row such as [1, 2, 3], with each number kept in its numbered slot

scaled-accumulation.definition: add a scalar multiple of one vector into another, out[i] += scale * values[i]
scaled-accumulation.intuition: multiply every incoming entry by one scale, then add each result into the matching output slot

previews.0: parts list
previews.1: the rows of notes amended, never replaced, by each block

residual-stream.definition: the per-position state that blocks add corrections onto
residual-stream.intuition: these very rows of notes as they flow through the model

previews.1: add the outcome back onto the stream

residual-addition.definition: out = a + b elementwise; the highway mechanism
residual-addition.intuition: each block's output is an edit added on; part of every training signal crosses untouched

previews.0: parts list
previews.1: ask, advertise, average across visible positions

attention.definition: score each query against visible keys, turn the scores into attention weights, and use those weights to average the values
attention.intuition: the one step where positions consult each other: ask, advertise, average

previews.1: question, advertisement, cargo

query-key-value.definition: three vectors per position produced together by one matmul: a query to match, a key to match against, and a value to carry

scaled-dot-product.definition: the dot product of two equal-length vectors divided by the square root of their length
scaled-dot-product.intuition: divide a query-key score by the spread that grows with the square root of the row width

previews.1: one temporary mixing share assigned to a visible position

attention-weight.definition: one softmax probability assigned to a visible position's value
attention-weight.intuition: the share of the answer borrowed from one visible position's cargo

previews.1: mix visible value rows using non-negative shares that sum to one

weighted-average.definition: sum vectors after multiplying each by a non-negative weight, where all weights sum to one
weighted-average.intuition: each consulted position contributes its assigned share of cargo to the output

previews.0: parts list
previews.1: independent copy of attention on a 32-channel slice

head.definition: one of H attention computations confined to its own channel slice
head.intuition: one independent copy of the consulting routine on its own 32-channel slice

head-size.definition: C/H, the equal channel count assigned to each attention group
head-size.intuition: split four toy channels into two equal groups of two; the default split is 128 into four groups of 32

block.definition: the repeated unit that adds one edit made by consulting visible rows and a second edit made within each row
block.intuition: one stage gives the continuing notes two edits: consult earlier rows and then work within each row

pre-norm.definition: prepare a steadied copy before each block branch, then add the branch's edit to the unmodified continuing state
pre-norm.intuition: the editor reads a steadied copy while the original notes continue along the highway

previews.0: choose one character, append it, and run again; Chapter 1 builds the loop

autoregressive.definition: write one token at a time, feed it back, and choose again from the preceding context available to the model
autoregressive.intuition: during a generation call, choose one character, append it to the visible text, and predict again without adjusting parameters

previews.0: name in the parts list; Chapter 1 builds the no-peeking rule

causality.definition: a prediction at position t may depend only on positions 0 through t, never later positions
causality.intuition: no peeking: the next character is the very answer the bet is graded on

previews.1: bet sheet: 80 non-negative numbers summing to 1
previews.0: route preview: next-character probabilities, with Chapter 5 as the construction

probability-distribution.definition: one non-negative number per possible choice, with all of the numbers summing to one
probability-distribution.intuition: the bet sheet: 80 non-negative numbers that sum to 1

previews.1: raw scores before softmax

logits.definition: one unconstrained raw score per vocabulary entry and position
logits.intuition: the raw scores before they are squashed into a bet sheet

previews.1: squashing machinery, scores to probabilities

softmax.definition: subtract a score row's maximum, exponentiate each shifted score, then divide by their sum to make a distribution
softmax.intuition: the squashing machinery that turns scores into a bet sheet

softmax-saturation.definition: as score gaps grow, softmax probabilities crowd toward one for the winner and zero for the others
softmax-saturation.intuition: a score far ahead takes nearly the whole bet sheet and leaves almost no share for the rest

log-sum-exp.definition: maximum + log(sum(exp(score[i] - maximum))), an overflow-resistant way to compute the log of summed exponentials
log-sum-exp.intuition: subtract the tallest score before exponentiating, then put that shared height back after the logarithm

previews.1: grades the batch with one number

cross-entropy.definition: the batch mean of -log(probability assigned to each correct next token)
cross-entropy.intuition: one number grading the batch: the penalty for weak bets on the truth

previews.0: parts list
previews.1: id fetches its learned row; plus a position row

embedding.definition: look up one learned token vector by id and add the learned vector for that position to make the starting notes
embedding.intuition: each id fetches its learned row: the position's opening notes, identity plus location

previews.1: T x C learned rows, one per position

position-table.definition: a learned table with one vector for each position up to the configured block size; a call with time T uses positions zero through T - 1
position-table.intuition: the learned where-am-I row added into every opening note

parameter-registry.definition: one flat array containing one pointer to every Param object owned by the model
parameter-registry.intuition: named fields say what each learned object does while one exactly-once list lets whole-model chores reach every object

canonical-parameter-order.definition: the fixed sequence of Param objects shared by construction, seeded random draws, generic model loops, and later checkpoint bytes
canonical-parameter-order.intuition: one stable numbered ledger keeps every whole-model consumer from inventing a different order

chained-assignment.definition: a C expression with adjacent assignments grouped from right to left, where the inner assignment's stored value becomes the outer assignment's value
chained-assignment.intuition: one constructor returns one Param pointer, then the registry slot and readable named field receive that same address

previews.8: navigation title for Chapter 9, where the supplied internal layout is constructed

private-model-blueprint.definition: the exact internal Model and Block structure declarations shared by separately compiled model implementation files
private-model-blueprint.intuition: every implementation file must calculate the same field offset from Model *, so the supplied internal header is byte-exact

previews.0: parts list (tied embeddings)
previews.1: token table reused as output scoreboard
previews.5: final prediction head reuses the token table as its weights; Chapter 9 constructs the arrangement
previews.6: output matmul and embedding contributions meet in the same token-table gradient; Chapter 9 constructs the arrangement

tied-head.definition: one token-table Param supplies both opening lookup rows and the weight rows used to score the final notes
tied-head.intuition: one token-table object is both the input dictionary and output scoreboard, so both jobs share values, gradients, and optimizer history

previews.1: full-capacity working buffers are reused across calls; Chapter 10 owns their storage plan
previews.5: future allocation that will hold temporary forward and backward views; Chapter 10 constructs its placement
previews.9: literal values_arena and gradient_arena fields reserved in the supplied private layout; Chapter 10 constructs their storage plan

arena.definition: one owned contiguous float allocation whose disjoint ranges back many non-owning views; Tiny AgenC uses one for forward values and one for activation gradients
arena.intuition: one float array is divided by exact numeric offsets, and each Mat view exposes one non-overlapping range

previews.4: model dimensions will receive a checked memory calculation before allocation
previews.8: one Param demonstrates fixed bounds-before-product guards
previews.9: Chapter 10 is named as owner of the checked whole-model byte calculation

checked-memory-size-arithmetic.definition: compute size_t sums and products only after proving the result is at most SIZE_MAX, returning failure instead of allowing wraparound
checked-memory-size-arithmetic.intuition: check left at most SIZE_MAX minus right before addition, and left zero or right at most SIZE_MAX divided by left before multiplication

previews.9: model_memory.c is identified as measuring and placing temporary storage

two-pass-arena-layout.definition: run one fixed placement sequence with a NULL base to count floats, allocate that capacity, then run the same sequence with the real base to assign every view
two-pass-arena-layout.intuition: for a two-by-two view followed by one-by-three, the counting pass advances from zero to four to seven and the placement pass assigns starts zero and four

previews.0: the first-run banner shows one reserved-working-memory total
previews.1: the activation count previews full-capacity storage and the T-squared attention area
previews.9: legal geometry is separated from representable storage before Chapter 10 constructs the report

model-memory-report.definition: an allocation-free checked report of parameter-buffer bytes, value-arena bytes, activation-gradient bytes, two cached-id buffers, and their total
model-memory-report.intuition: four named large-buffer subtotals are calculated before allocation; small structures, pointer arrays, and allocator overhead are excluded

previews.1: the activation ledger keeps one trip's working values for its matching backward pass
previews.6: saved values must describe the matching forward call
previews.9: the private blueprint reserves ids, active shape, target status, and top-level activation views
previews.10: one reusable arena and two id buffers hold the contents that the next forward call replaces

latest-forward-record.definition: the model-owned record for the newest forward call: active shape, copied token ids, targets when supplied, target status, and the saved values that belong to a matching backward call; every later forward replaces its applicability
latest-forward-record.intuition: one activation ledger belongs to one trip through the notes; a new trip rewrites the ledger even when some old bytes remain

inference-mode.definition: a target-free model_forward call that runs the shared score route through logits, skips fresh probabilities and loss, returns a zero no-loss sentinel, and replaces the latest-forward record with one that must not feed backward
inference-mode.intuition: run the shared route without an answer sheet, leaving raw next-character scores for a later caller but making no bet, grade, correction, or character choice

previews.1: the reverse map previews returning corrections; Chapter 12 assembles the exact source route
previews.6: the complete local derivative ledger previews the model-scale call order
previews.9: the tied table and registry preview model-wide gradient destinations
previews.10: the activation-gradient arena and stream selectors prepare the shared destinations
previews.11: the latest target-bearing record prepares the saved values that backward consumes

model-backward-wiring.definition: one source-ordered reverse traversal of the newest target-bearing forward record, starting from cleared destinations, walking blocks from L-1 to zero, and accumulating at residual and tied paths
model-backward-wiring.intuition: read the notes highway backward and add every returning correction into the matching lane where paths meet

parameter-connectivity-witness.definition: a fixed-fixture check that requires at least one finite nonzero gradient entry in every registered Param while making no claim that every coordinate or packed subregion is connected
parameter-connectivity-witness.intuition: inspect each registered parameter object for at least one returning correction, while admitting that a live entry can hide an unused neighbor in the same object

previews.1: matrix multiplication, the workhorse

matmul.definition: dot every input row with every weight row, computing out = x * W^T for weights stored as outputs by inputs
matmul.intuition: rows dotted with rows; every transform in the model is one of these

previews.1: multiply matching channels, add up

dot-product.definition: sum of elementwise products of two equal-length rows
dot-product.intuition: multiply matching entries, add them up

sum-notation.definition: Sigma as the math spelling of the accumulate loop
sum-notation.intuition: Sigma is the math spelling of the accumulate loop

previews.0: parts list (layer normalization)
previews.1: steady the stream's scale

layernorm.definition: subtract each row's mean, multiply by 1/sqrt(population variance + epsilon), then apply learned per-channel gain and bias
layernorm.intuition: centers and rescales each row; its learned volume knob starts neutral at gain one, bias zero

epsilon.definition: a small positive constant added at a division boundary so an otherwise zero divisor stays finite; layernorm uses 1e-5 inside its variance sum
epsilon.intuition: a tiny floor under a computed spread keeps division finite when the unguarded spread would be zero

mean-variance.definition: mean is the average; variance is mean squared distance from it; standard deviation is the square root of variance
mean-variance.intuition: find the center, average squared distances, then take a square root; independent variances add before that root

previews.0: parts list
previews.1: the smooth bend between the two MLP matmuls

gelu.intuition: the smooth bend between widen and narrow

nonlinearity.definition: a bend applied between matrix multiplications that cannot be collapsed into one linear transform
nonlinearity.intuition: without a bend, widen then narrow is still one matrix multiplication wearing two names

hyperbolic-tangent.definition: tanh(x) = (exp(2x) - 1) / (exp(2x) + 1), a smooth curve bounded between -1 and 1
hyperbolic-tangent.intuition: large negative inputs flatten near -1, zero stays zero, and large positive inputs flatten near 1

previews.1: widen, bend, narrow; the feed-forward layer
previews.0: parts list: GELU feed-forward layers

mlp.definition: a widening matrix multiplication, GELU, and a narrowing matrix multiplication
mlp.intuition: widen the notes, bend them, narrow them back

previews.1: a multiply-by-a-weight-matrix step; Chapter 5 constructs the multiplication

previews.0: loss-slope calculations are identified as Chapter 6 work
previews.1: a residual nudge moves the sum one-for-one; Chapter 6 names that rate

derivative.definition: the local rate at which one number changes when another receives an ever-smaller nudge
derivative.intuition: measure output change per unit input change as the nudge shrinks; a straight line keeps one rate while a bend has a rate at one point

partial-derivative.definition: a derivative with respect to one input while every other input is held fixed
partial-derivative.intuition: nudge one input alone, keep the other inputs fixed, and measure how the output responds

previews.0: gradient checker gloss in checkpoint
previews.1: correction signals pushed backward

gradient.definition: the shaped collection of the loss's partial derivatives with respect to a group of values
gradient.intuition: one loss-slope number beside every value; its sign gives a direction and its size gives the local sensitivity

previews.1: shared input and parameter gradients add every returning contribution; Chapter 6 builds the arithmetic

gradient-accumulation.definition: add every valid returning path's contribution into a shared gradient destination instead of replacing earlier contributions
gradient-accumulation.intuition: when paths meet, += keeps every returning contribution in the same destination

previews.0: follow one change through the next; Chapter 6 builds the arithmetic
previews.1: the reverse-map preview points to Chapter 6 for slopes and the chain rule

chain-rule.definition: multiply local derivatives along a consecutive path of dependent calculations
chain-rule.intuition: follow one small change through the next calculation by multiplying how strongly each stage responds

product-rule.definition: when two changing factors are multiplied, add the derivative contribution from changing each factor while holding the other fixed
product-rule.intuition: a product can change through either factor, so both routes contribute to its local slope

power-rule.definition: for the positive whole-number and reciprocal powers used here, the derivative of x^n is n times x^(n-1)
power-rule.intuition: x multiplied by itself n times has n equal routes for a nudge to change the product

quotient-rule.definition: for changing numerator a and denominator b, the derivative of a/b is (b times the derivative of a minus a times the derivative of b) divided by b squared
quotient-rule.intuition: numerator changes move a quotient in the same direction; denominator changes move it in the opposite direction and bring another denominator factor

exponential-derivative.definition: the derivative of exp(x) is exp(x)
exponential-derivative.intuition: the exponential's local slope equals its current height

logarithm-derivative.definition: for positive x, the derivative of log(x) is 1/x
logarithm-derivative.intuition: log undoes exponential growth, so its slope shrinks in inverse proportion to its positive input

tanh-derivative.definition: the derivative of tanh(x) is 1 minus tanh(x) squared
tanh-derivative.intuition: tanh climbs fastest near zero and flattens as its value approaches either bound

hadamard-product.definition: multiply matching entries of two equal-length vectors and keep each product as a vector entry
hadamard-product.intuition: pair each numbered slot with the same slot, as in a dot product, but keep the separate products instead of adding them

jacobian.definition: a matrix whose row i, column j holds the partial derivative of output i with respect to input j
jacobian.intuition: write every output-against-input slope in a small grid; backward applies the grid's effect without storing the grid

previews.0: parts list
previews.1: same diagram read bottom-to-top

backpropagation.definition: traverse the saved forward operations in reverse, multiply each arriving gradient by local derivatives, and accumulate where paths meet
backpropagation.intuition: read the forward diagram bottom-to-top, sending correction signals backward and collecting every valid path

previews.6: an independent nudge-based check compares observed loss response with the handwritten backward result

finite-differences.definition: estimate a local slope from small nonzero input nudges evaluated through the forward calculation
finite-differences.intuition: ask nearby forward values how quickly one scalar changes without reading a handwritten derivative formula

one-sided-difference.definition: estimate a derivative from the value at x and one nearby value f(x + h)
one-sided-difference.intuition: the slope from x to x plus h includes the curve's bend across that whole interval

central-difference.definition: estimate a derivative as (f(x + h) - f(x - h)) / (2*h), using equal nudges on both sides
central-difference.intuition: measure across a balanced interval so matching bend error on the two sides cancels

truncation-error.definition: the derivative-estimate error left by using a nonzero interval in place of the limiting local slope
truncation-error.intuition: a finite-width interval includes some of the curve beyond the one-point slope

second-order-error.definition: an error whose leading size is bounded by a constant times h squared for sufficiently small h, written O(h^2)
second-order-error.intuition: divide the nudge by ten and the leading truncation error falls by about one hundred

floating-point-cancellation.definition: loss of useful significant digits when nearly equal rounded floating-point values are subtracted
floating-point-cancellation.intuition: the matching leading digits disappear, leaving a small difference with fewer reliable digits

random-projection.definition: map a vector or matrix to one scalar by taking its dot product with one fixed randomly drawn vector
random-projection.intuition: one fixed row u turns every output entry into part of one measurable scalar, while backward receives that same u

mixed-tolerance.definition: accept two floats when their absolute difference is no larger than an absolute floor plus a relative allowance times their larger magnitude
mixed-tolerance.intuition: the fixed floor protects slopes near zero while the proportional part grows with larger slopes

known-answer-forward-test.definition: run forward on a fully specified small input and compare its result with an independently worked expected value
known-answer-forward-test.intuition: if the intended square at two should return four, a consistently differentiated cubic still fails by returning eight

derivative-check.definition: compare a backward calculation's analytic gradient with finite-difference slopes of the forward calculation within a stated tolerance
derivative-check.intuition: let backward claim each slope, let nearby forward measurements answer independently, and make the mixed tolerance referee the pair

function-pointer-callback.definition: a function pointer stores which compatible function to call; a function invoked later through that supplied pointer serves as a callback
function-pointer-callback.intuition: give the common nudge loop one operation-specific measure function to call without copying the loop

designated-struct-initializer.definition: a brace list whose .field = value entries initialize named struct fields without relying on declaration order; omitted fields begin at zero
designated-struct-initializer.intuition: fill the GELU case's out, projection, and input fields by name while unrelated case fields begin at zero

bounded-formatted-output.definition: snprintf formats values into a character buffer while respecting a supplied byte capacity, including the terminating zero byte
bounded-formatted-output.intuition: build model param followed by an index inside a 32-byte label array without writing beyond it

activation.definition: any value the forward pass computes, as opposed to learned parameters
activation.intuition: working contents recomputed for one trip while their allocated storage is reused, not a learned parameter

tensor.definition: umbrella word for any shaped collection of numbers
tensor.intuition: one word covering matrices, rows, and collections with more dimensions

transpose.definition: the same grid read with rows and columns swapped
transpose.intuition: the same grid with rows and columns swapped

module.definition: a group of C files and functions responsible for one contract
module.intuition: one named part of the program with one job and a public boundary

pointer.definition: a C value that stores an address
pointer.intuition: an address held in a value so code can reach another object

size-t.definition: C's unsigned integer type for object sizes, element counts, and byte counts
size-t.intuition: move dimension arithmetic into the type C uses to count objects before multiplying

struct.definition: C's way to group named fields into one value
struct.intuition: one value made from named slots

opaque-handle.definition: a pointer to a representation hidden behind a module's public functions
opaque-handle.intuition: the caller holds the address while the module guards the private fields

value-type.definition: a public struct whose complete description is copied by assignment
value-type.intuition: copy the small public description itself, not a hidden object

function-module.definition: a module with functions but no mutable private state kept between calls
function-module.intuition: a named toolbox whose functions keep no hidden mutable object

allocation.definition: request a block of bytes and receive its address or failure
allocation.intuition: ask for a block of bytes before any pointer can refer to model storage

null-pointer.definition: the special C pointer value NULL that means no address
null-pointer.intuition: malloc returns the no-address value when it cannot supply a block

sizeof.definition: the C operator that reports how many bytes an object type occupies
sizeof.intuition: inspect the pointed-to type for its byte size without following the pointer or reading the object

type-alias.definition: a second C name for a type, introduced with typedef
type-alias.intuition: give the three file-status outcomes one type name instead of passing an unexplained integer

preprocessor-macro.definition: a name or condition handled by C's preprocessor before ordinary compilation
preprocessor-macro.intuition: define the requested POSIX interface names before system headers are read

file-private-static.definition: static on a file-scope C function or object keeps that name private to the current C file
file-private-static.intuition: the utility file owns its clock constant and the RNG file owns its state-step helper without exporting either name

logical-or.definition: the C || operator is true when either condition is true and checks its left side first
logical-or.intuition: reject the call when either required output address is missing

const-qualification.definition: const prevents code from changing an object through the qualified name or pointer
const-qualification.intuition: die may read the format characters through its pointer but promises not to rewrite them

pointer-member-access.definition: the C -> operator follows a struct pointer and accesses one named field
pointer-member-access.intuition: rng->state follows the private RNG handle to its state field

variadic-function.definition: a C function whose fixed arguments may be followed by extra arguments
variadic-function.intuition: die accepts one format string followed by the values that fill it

fixed-width-integer.definition: an integer type whose name states its exact bit count
fixed-width-integer.intuition: the type name fixes the bit count used by files and PCG arithmetic

native-byte-order.definition: the machine's ordering of an integer's bytes from least-significant first or most-significant first
native-byte-order.intuition: on common eight-bit-byte machines, one is 01 00 00 00 or 00 00 00 01; the helpers copy those bytes unchanged

unsigned-wraparound.intuition: when an unsigned counter passes its largest bit pattern, it wraps to zero

bitwise-operations.definition: shift, XOR, OR, and AND operate on individual bits of an integer
bitwise-operations.intuition: fold distant old-state bits with XOR, rotate them with shifts, then join and mask the pieces

previews.0: exact generated text can depend on floating-point behavior; Chapter 2 builds the representation limit
previews.1: four-byte activation storage

float-precision.definition: the supported IEEE 754 float carries 24 significant binary bits; compiler, math-library, and operation-order differences can change the last bits
float-precision.intuition: keep the 24 PCG bits a float can distinguish; later last-bit arithmetic differences can steer a generated-text choice

previews.1: negative infinity as the conventional future-position mask that this source does not use

nonfinite-float.definition: IEEE floating-point markers outside finite numbers: positive and negative infinity represent overflow directions, while NaN marks arithmetic with no real-number answer
nonfinite-float.intuition: infinity minus infinity has no real-number answer, so a softmax row containing that subtraction becomes NaN instead of a bet sheet

thread.definition: one separately scheduled path of instructions through a program; threads in that program share its memory
thread.intuition: several workers can read shared inputs at once, but safe parallel loops give each worker a separate output row

previews.0: optional build support that spreads selected independent loops across CPU cores

openmp.definition: compiler and runtime support for assigning selected C loop iterations to CPU threads when their writes are disjoint
openmp.intuition: give independent loop iterations to several CPU workers

data-race.definition: two unsynchronized threads access the same memory at the same time and at least one access writes, which gives C undefined behavior
data-race.intuition: two workers may read the same input, but each must own a separate output row or slice

ownership-lifetime.definition: the caller responsible for one allocated block may use it until freeing it exactly once
ownership-lifetime.intuition: the caller receives the block, uses it while alive, and ends its lifetime with one free

monotonic-clock.definition: a clock for elapsed durations whose readings do not move backward
monotonic-clock.intuition: elapsed-time ticks that civil-time corrections cannot turn backward

previews.1: programmer contract violations stop at the broken internal rule

assertion.definition: a removable C check for an internal programmer contract that stops an assertion-enabled build when false
assertion.intuition: a zero bound names no possible answer, so the caller contract requires bound greater than zero

do-while-loop.definition: a C loop that executes its body once before checking whether to repeat
do-while-loop.intuition: make one bounded draw, inspect its low word, and repeat only if it lies in the uneven edge

linear-congruential.definition: advance integer state with multiply, add, and fixed-width wraparound
linear-congruential.intuition: the hand-checkable state rule: multiply, add, wrap, repeat

pcg32.definition: a 64-bit congruential state step permuted into 32 output bits
pcg32.intuition: the raw low bits repeat early, so fold distant old-state bits with XOR and rotate them into a 32-bit draw

bounded-random.definition: an unbiased integer draw in [0, bound) made by multiply-high and rejection
bounded-random.intuition: split the product into high and low words, reject low words below 2^32 mod range, then return the high word

sine-cosine.definition: cosine and sine give the horizontal and vertical coordinates of an angle on a circle
sine-cosine.intuition: the unit-circle turn table gives horizontal cosine and vertical sine; multiply both by the radius

squared-distance.definition: perpendicular coordinates x and y have squared radius r*r = x*x + y*y
squared-distance.intuition: four 3-by-4 right triangles leave an inner square of area 25, so the slanted distance is 5

circle-angle.definition: an angle records direction; radians measure it by arc length so one full turn is 2*pi
circle-angle.intuition: zero, quarter, half, and three-quarter turns point right, up, left, and down

previews.0: seeded choices that can be replayed
previews.1: random initial weights and corpus snippets

randomness.definition: repeatable pseudorandom sequences used for initialization, batch choice, and generated-text choices
randomness.intuition: each job owns a seeded handle; equal seeds replay while advancing one handle cannot move another

uniform-random.definition: one of exactly 2^24 fractions k/2^24 in [0, 1), each backed by 256 PCG32 outputs
uniform-random.intuition: keep the 24 high bits a float can distinguish and scale the equally represented grid from 0 through 1 - 2^-24

independence.definition: learning one random choice does not change the chances assigned to another
independence.intuition: every pair of two balanced sign choices occurs, so fixing the first leaves the second's chances unchanged

previews.1: bell-curve noise with spread sigma

gaussian.definition: the ideal mean-zero, standard-deviation-one bell rule; rng_gaussian is its 24-bit Box-Muller approximation
gaussian.intuition: equal-area rings turn an exponential tail into a radius; the finite uniform grid caps that radius near 5.7681

previews.0: the mechanism that uses gradients to adjust parameters; Chapter 8 constructs it
previews.1: the updater that turns gradients into parameter changes

optimizer.definition: a rule with settings and optional persistent state that turns computed gradients into parameter changes
optimizer.intuition: the current gradient supplies one direction signal; settings and optional history determine the optimizer's actual move

learning-rate.definition: the nonnegative multiplier that controls the distance of a parameter update
learning-rate.intuition: the update rule chooses a direction and the learning rate scales the distance moved along it

stochastic-gradient-descent.definition: subtract learning rate times the current batch gradient from each parameter
stochastic-gradient-descent.intuition: take a scaled downhill step using the correction signal estimated from one randomly drawn batch

exponential-moving-average.definition: a running history equal to beta times its old value plus 1 - beta times the newest observation
exponential-moving-average.intuition: each new observation gets the largest fresh vote while every older vote fades by another factor of beta

momentum.definition: use a fading average of gradients to carry recent direction between optimizer steps
momentum.intuition: recent batch directions keep a fading vote instead of the latest batch replacing them outright

first-moment.definition: Adam's exponential moving average of the signed gradient at one scalar coordinate
first-moment.intuition: a fading signed history records which direction recent gradients have repeatedly requested

second-raw-moment.definition: Adam's exponential moving average of squared gradients at one scalar coordinate, without subtracting a mean
second-raw-moment.intuition: square each gradient to keep its size but remove its sign, then retain a fading size history for that coordinate

adaptive-scaling.definition: divide each coordinate's signed gradient history by sqrt(its squared-gradient history) + epsilon
adaptive-scaling.intuition: measure each requested move in units of that same coordinate's recent gradient size

bias-correction.definition: divide a zero-started exponential moving average by its accumulated coefficient mass 1 - beta^step so the weights renormalize to one
bias-correction.intuition: the artificial zero start leaves the observed weights summing below one, so rescale their accumulated total back to one

adam-optimizer.definition: an optimizer that bias-corrects signed and squared-gradient moving averages, then uses their ratio to scale every parameter coordinate
adam-optimizer.intuition: carry recent direction, measure it against that coordinate's recent gradient size, and use the corrected ratio for the next move

weight-decay.definition: a learning-rate-scaled pull that moves selected parameter values directly toward zero
weight-decay.intuition: subtract a stated fraction of the current value directly instead of sending that pull through adaptive gradient scaling

previews.0: parts-list label with Chapter 8 as the construction
previews.1: the mechanism that turns gradients into parameter nudges

adamw-optimizer.definition: Adam with selected weight decay applied outside the adaptive gradient fraction
adamw-optimizer.intuition: make Adam's history-scaled move, then include a separately sized direct pull toward zero

param-object.definition: the opaque C object that owns one matrix-shaped value region and same-shaped gradient, first-moment, and second-moment regions
param-object.intuition: four aligned regions keep every learned value beside its correction signal and both pieces of optimizer history

gradient-norm.definition: the square root of the sum of every squared parameter-gradient entry
gradient-norm.intuition: collapse the complete gradient vector to one length while retaining its direction separately

gradient-clipping.definition: when the global gradient norm exceeds its cap, multiply every parameter gradient by the same cap divided by that norm
gradient-clipping.intuition: one shared scale shortens an oversized model-wide gradient without changing the ratios among its coordinates

previews.0: exp and log named as math the book will build

exponential.definition: exp(x) = e^x, where e is the limiting factor from increasingly fine compounded growth
exponential.intuition: split one stated increase into finer compounded updates, check whole and half powers of the limiting factor, then name exp

previews.0: exp and log named as math the book will build

logarithm.definition: the inverse of exp on positive inputs
logarithm.intuition: log answers which exponent made a positive exponential output

previews.0: controls how varied the generated choices are
previews.14: positive command value passed through to the Chapter 16 choice mechanism
previews.15: deferred scaling inside the opaque post-update progress-text hook

temperature.definition: a finite positive value that divides each logit's gap from the row maximum before softmax, widening the gaps below one and narrowing them above one
temperature.intuition: a positive denominator on gaps in the bet sheet's raw scores: a smaller denominator stretches the gaps and concentrates the shares, while a larger one compresses them

previews.0: sample command chooses the next characters
previews.1: weighted-die choice from the next-character bet sheet
previews.14: opaque generation operation whose checkpoint, prompt, length, temperature, seed, and output route are checked here
previews.15: opaque post-update progress-text hook; Chapter 16 constructs the draw and append mechanism

sampling.definition: lay one half-open interval per vocabulary id with width equal to its probability, place one finite uniform draw, and choose the first id whose running boundary exceeds that draw
sampling.intuition: lay the bet-sheet shares along the interval from zero to one, place one available uniform draw, append the id under it, and make a new bet sheet

previews.1: generation uses the newest T ids after a prefix exceeds the model's context capacity
previews.15: deferred newest-suffix selection inside the opaque progress-text hook

sliding-context-window.definition: once a generated prefix reaches context capacity, move its visible starting address so each next-token call receives the newest block_size ids and no older id
sliding-context-window.intuition: move the visible strip's left edge after it fills so the next bet sheet is built from the newest T ids

baseline.definition: a simpler prediction rule scored with the same loss on the same target positions as the model under judgment
baseline.intuition: give a simpler answerer the same flashcards; extra machinery earns credit only when its grade is lower on those questions

bigram.definition: an ordered pair of adjacent tokens; a bigram count predictor groups next-token counts by the pair's first token
bigram.intuition: cover every flashcard question except its final visible character, then tally which answer followed that character in training

add-one-smoothing.definition: add one provisional count to every vocabulary outcome before normalizing, so every possible next token retains positive probability
add-one-smoothing.intuition: start every line of the bigram bet sheet with one counter before adding observed transitions

perplexity.definition: exp of mean next-token loss, interpreted as the number of equal-probability choices whose uniform loss would be the same
perplexity.intuition: replace the changing bet sheets with one equally split sheet that would receive the same average grade, then count its lines

previews.0: pins the randomness for reproducibility

seed.definition: the caller's starting value incorporated by the generator's fixed entry procedure
seed.intuition: the same starting value follows the same two-advance entry procedure and replays the draws

checkpoint-format-identity.definition: the TAGC version 1 agreement in which a native 32-bit magic value and version select one exact ordered header-and-payload byte layout
checkpoint-format-identity.intuition: in the 130-byte worked file, magic occupies 0..3, version 4..7, six dimensions 8..31, tokenizer count 32..35, AB 36..37, 22 floats 38..125, and the final check 126..129

checksum.definition: a stored fixed-size value recalculated from all preceding serialized bytes to detect accidental change
checksum.intuition: 01 02 and 00 03 both sum to 3, so a useful stored check must depend on bit positions rather than the ordinary byte total

crc32.definition: the reflected 32-bit cyclic redundancy check used here as a checksum: initial FFFFFFFF, byte XOR, eight right-shift and EDB88320 polynomial updates per byte, then final complement
crc32.intuition: for byte 41, the source rule moves FFFFFFBE through eight checkable states and complements 2C266174 to D3D99E8B

authentication.definition: evidence that accepted bytes came from a trusted creator rather than merely matching an unkeyed accidental-change check
authentication.intuition: an editor can change checkpoint bytes and recalculate CRC32, so a matching checksum cannot identify who made the file

checkpoint-resource-preflight.definition: an allocation-free load and save gate requiring valid geometry, at most one GiB of reported resident model memory, and an overflow-checked checkpoint size within the file ceiling before construction
checkpoint-resource-preflight.intuition: the valid V=1, T=1024, C=1, H=1, L=1, B=1024 header fits a 4,213-byte file but requests one 4-GiB attention-score region, so it is rejected before model_new

file-descriptor.definition: a nonnegative operating-system integer handle for an open file that remains live until it is closed or transferred to a stream
file-descriptor.intuition: mkstemp returns the integer handle; fdopen transfers it to FILE *, after which fclose closes both stream and descriptor

octal-integer-literal.definition: a C integer literal whose leading zero makes the following digits base eight
octal-integer-literal.intuition: each 7 in 0777 contributes three one bits, so three digits select nine permission bits

file-permission-bits.definition: the owner, group, and other read, write, and execute bits selected from st_mode and applied to an open file by fchmod
file-permission-bits.intuition: existing.st_mode & 0777 keeps only three read-write-execute triplets; this writer copies those bits but not ownership, access-control lists, or other metadata

atomic-file-replacement.definition: write and close a complete adjacent temporary file, then rename it over the destination in one same-filesystem directory-entry operation
atomic-file-replacement.intuition: a concurrent opener sees complete model A before rename or complete model B after rename, never half-written B

previews.0: a saved-model file such as trained.bin; Chapter 13 builds and names the format
previews.1: the saved boundary between parameter-changing training and fixed-parameter generation

checkpoint.definition: the self-contained saved-model handoff that records format identity, model dimensions, the canonical tokenizer alphabet, and learned parameter values with an accidental-change check so a later process can reconstruct the model
checkpoint.intuition: the 130-byte worked checkpoint restores geometry, alphabet, and 22 learned floats; gradients, AdamW moments and step, RNG position, corpus position, arenas, and cached forward state remain outside version 1

checkpoint-durability.definition: this implementation's bounded persistence promise: fsync the completed temporary file and atomically replace the runtime name, without claiming parent-directory synchronization or universal power-loss survival
checkpoint-durability.intuition: fsync covers the temporary file's contents; rename changes the visible name; no parent-directory fsync means sudden-power-loss survival remains filesystem-dependent

fatal-error-policy.definition: the command-line process policy implemented by die: prefix one fatal diagnostic, write it to standard error, and end without returning
fatal-error-policy.intuition: when required storage or state is unavailable, report the reason once at the shared wrapper instead of letting each caller improvise or continue without a model

bounded-file-read.definition: read an entire file only when its measured length fits a caller-supplied ceiling and representable sentinel allocation, returning distinct success, I/O-error, and too-large outcomes
bounded-file-read.intuition: measure the file against the caller's ceiling, reject an oversized body before allocating or reading it, and publish owned bytes plus their exact length only after a complete read

argument-vector.definition: the argc count and argv ordered array of zero-terminated command strings supplied to main
argument-vector.intuition: the six shell words in ./tiny-agenc train --data tiny.txt --steps 12 arrive in numbered slots zero through five; shifting the pointer gives the chosen parser a smaller view beginning at train

process-exit-status.definition: the process result returned to the invoking shell or script, with success for a completed request and failure for a refused or incomplete one
process-exit-status.intuition: when allocation makes the command unable to continue, die reaches exit(EXIT_FAILURE) once and no caller can accidentally resume after the fatal diagnostic

command-line-dispatch.definition: select exactly one command grammar from the first argument, or answer an exact top-level information form or reject the request
command-line-dispatch.intuition: the required train or sample grammar removes the guesswork that a flat mixture of corpus, checkpoint, learning, and prompt flags would create

conversion-end-pointer.definition: the address a C string-to-number converter writes for the first byte it did not consume
conversion-end-pointer.intuition: strtol can return 12 for 12oops, but the pointer landing on o exposes that the requested integer did not use the whole string

errno-range-signal.definition: the reset-call-check protocol in which a library conversion records an out-of-range result by setting errno to ERANGE
errno-range-signal.intuition: clear yesterday's library error to zero, call strtoull, then accept the range signal only if that call changed errno to ERANGE

whole-string-numeric-parsing.definition: convert a command string only when it is nonempty, every byte is consumed by the value's grammar, and the result satisfies that flag's range policy
whole-string-numeric-parsing.intuition: a useful numeric prefix is still a bad command value: 12 ends at the zero byte and passes, while 12oops leaves o behind and fails

command-line-option-parsing.definition: start one typed command record from defaults, replace its fields from recognized options in encounter order, reject leftovers, then hand off the completed record
command-line-option-parsing.intuition: both --steps 20 --data tiny.txt and the reverse order fill the same TrainOptions fields before any training work begins

file-metadata-query.definition: the stat call that resolves a path and fills a struct stat record with operating-system metadata about the existing filesystem object
file-metadata-query.intuition: before replacing a checkpoint, stat fills existing.st_mode so the adjacent temporary can preserve the destination's permission bits; failure leaves the private creation mode in place

filesystem-link-alias.definition: distinct path text that identifies the same existing filesystem object, either as another hard-link name or by resolving a symbolic link
filesystem-link-alias.intuition: corpus.txt and corpus-link.txt have different spelling, yet stat can resolve both to device 8 and inode 42017

filesystem-object-identity.definition: equality of the device and inode metadata returned when two existing path names are resolved by stat
filesystem-object-identity.intuition: corpus.txt and corpus-link.txt can have different spelling yet resolve to the same device-and-inode pair; the CLI conservatively requires output, training, and validation roles to name distinct objects before work begins

command-setup-preflight.definition: stage recoverable path, corpus, vocabulary, geometry, and model-memory checks before model construction and the long-running command body
command-setup-preflight.intuition: narrow checked options through path aliases, bounded bytes, one shared alphabet, complete windows, compatible geometry, and a model-buffer report before model_new

sample-command-setup.definition: load a checkpoint and tokenizer, prepare a newline plus known prompt ids and a seeded RNG, then hand checked bounds and objects to the still-opaque sampling operation
sample-command-setup.intuition: the checkpoint supplies a matched model and alphabet; one reserved newline and all known prompt bytes precede the requested generated tail, while Chapter 16 owns how each new id is chosen

cli-stream-routing.definition: the public assignment of generated text and successful information or narration to standard output, and diagnostics or the sampling banner to standard error
cli-stream-routing.intuition: redirecting sample stdout writes only continuation text while the architecture banner remains visible on stderr

line-buffering-request.definition: the best-effort setvbuf request that asks standard output to send completed training lines onward without waiting for a large full buffer
line-buffering-request.intuition: a person tailing a redirected training log should receive each newline-terminated progress report while the run is active, although this program ignores a setvbuf failure

environment-variable-lookup.definition: use getenv to ask whether an inherited environment name is present, receiving a pointer to its text value or NULL when absent without validating that value
environment-variable-lookup.intuition: OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 supplies an operator choice to one run; a non-null getenv result tells Tiny AgenC to leave interpretation and thread selection to the OpenMP runtime

runtime-thread-default.definition: the program's OpenMP fallback that requests half the reported available processors only when OMP_NUM_THREADS is absent and the half is positive
runtime-thread-default.intuition: the measured 64-thread machine performed better with 32, but any environment choice belongs to the operator and suppresses the program fallback

switch-statement.definition: a C multiway selection in which one switch value chooses a matching case or the default branch, and break prevents execution from continuing into the next case
switch-statement.intuition: the compact letter returned by getopt_long selects exactly one TrainOptions assignment; break leaves that assignment branch before the next label

command-line-boundary.definition: the bidirectional layer that narrows untrusted command words, paths, and environment through typed parsing and defensive setup, refuses detected problems, routes successful output and diagnostics, and returns a process status
command-line-boundary.intuition: 12oops, known file aliases, unknown validation bytes, and impossible memory requests are refused before long-running work; admitted paths and text still face their owning file, checkpoint, and tokenizer checks, while generated text and diagnostics leave on separate streams

remainder-operator.definition: the C percent operator on integers, which returns the remainder left after division and therefore returns zero for an exact multiple
remainder-operator.intuition: four divides into groups of two with nothing left, so 4 % 2 is zero and the geometry divides evenly

previews.0: the repeated batch-to-update cycle that Chapter 15 will close
previews.12: the caller that will place zero, forward, backward, and update in the verified order
previews.14: the long-running body that replaces the learner-only no-update scaffold

training-loop.definition: the repeated command-level sequence that draws one batch, clears gradient destinations, runs one target-bearing forward and its immediately matching backward, applies one checked model update, then performs due observation work only after that update
training-loop.intuition: deal one batch of flashcards, erase old correction marks, grade it, send corrections back, move the adjustable numbers, then deal again

fixed-batch-memorization-test.definition: reuse one unchanged input-and-target batch through many training steps and require finite loss to fall sharply, as an assembled-learning-path witness rather than a held-out quality claim
fixed-batch-memorization-test.intuition: show the same small stack of flashcards until the model can remember them; failure exposes a broken learning path, while success says nothing about unseen cards

previews.3: Chapter 15 will draw validation windows once and reuse them across reports

fixed-validation-batches.definition: a small collection of held-out input-and-target windows drawn once from a dedicated seeded RNG and reused at every validation report
fixed-validation-batches.intuition: deal held-aside flashcards once and keep those same cards on the desk so report-to-report changes come from the model rather than new cards

held-out-evaluation.definition: measure mean loss on held-aside examples with target-bearing forward calls but no backward call or parameter update
held-out-evaluation.intuition: grade the fixed cards behind the no-peeking line, record the grade, and never send its corrections back

generalization.definition: predictive improvement learned from update-eligible examples also reduces loss on examples withheld from updates
generalization.intuition: corrections learned from the training-side flashcards also improve grades on cards kept behind the no-peeking boundary

overfitting.definition: continued improvement on training examples that does not transfer to held-out examples, observed when training loss falls while held-out loss stalls or rises
overfitting.intuition: the model remembers details on the allowed flashcards while its grades stop improving on cards behind the no-peeking line

training-observation-isolation.definition: reporting, held-out measurement, progress text, and checkpoint saves run only after the current update and neither consume the batch RNG nor apply another parameter update
training-observation-isolation.intuition: inspect a completed step from a separate desk, then draw the next training flashcards from the untouched batch handle

previews.0: the ms/step estimate whose exact timed region Chapter 15 will open

training-step-timing.definition: the mean elapsed time per completed core training step since the last clock reset, stopped before validation and reporting and reset after every excluded side effect
training-step-timing.intuition: time only completed batch-to-update cycles, then restart the stopwatch after inspection, progress text, or file output

trigram.definition: an ordered run of three adjacent tokens; in the capstone comparator the first two select a count row and the third is the next-token answer
trigram.intuition: use the previous two token ids, rather than one, as the address of the next-answer count row

backoff.definition: a fixed fallback from an unavailable longer-context count row to a shorter-context prediction rule
backoff.intuition: when the two-byte row is absent, consult the final byte's add-one bet sheet instead

previews.16: retain earlier key and value calculations before eviction; Appendix C owns the state-management construction

key-value-cache.definition: temporary inference state that retains each layer's earlier attention key and value rows so an unchanged prefix need not be projected again
key-value-cache.intuition: retain each earlier position's advertisement and cargo while the growing prefix leaves their meanings unchanged

rotary-position-embedding.definition: a position mechanism that rotates adjacent query and key channel pairs by scheduled angles inside each attention head
rotary-position-embedding.intuition: rotate each head's question and advertisement by their local positions so their match depends on the angle between them

previews.18: a variable-length-token capstone linked forward to Appendix C

byte-pair-encoding.definition: deterministic tokenization that repeatedly replaces the most frequent adjacent token pair and records the ranked merge program
byte-pair-encoding.intuition: replace recurring neighboring byte pieces with one reusable id, then replay the same ranked replacements on new bytes

previews.18: variable-length tokens require matched units for fair loss comparison; Appendix C builds the exact unit

nats-per-byte.definition: the total natural-log next-token penalty divided by the exact number of target bytes covered by those predicted tokens
nats-per-byte.intuition: add the complete penalty bill, count the bytes whose answers incurred it, and divide once

scaling-law.definition: an empirical relationship fitted across changes in model, data, or training scale under declared measurement rules
scaling-law.intuition: many controlled measurements can trace a recurring size-to-result relationship; three tiny widths supply only three local points

median.definition: the middle value after an odd-sized collection of measurements has been sorted
median.intuition: put repeated timings in order and select the one with the same number of timings on either side

notes.summary: rows are the model's running notes about each position, amended never replaced

bet-sheet.summary: a probability distribution is an 80-line bet sheet on the next character

no-peeking.summary: the next character is the graded answer; no bet may read ahead

highway.summary: the residual stream is an unobstructed highway; blocks add edits, never rewrites

consulting.summary: attention as positions consulting each other: question, advertisement, cargo

volume-knob.summary: layernorm always normalizes; its learned gain-and-bias volume knob starts neutral

flashcards.summary: dataset windows are flashcards whose question is a token row and whose answer is the same row shifted forward
